- SLA targets: p95 < 120ms for chat responses, bulk embeddings within 2s for 10k batched requests.
- Security: must run dedicated capacity in our VPC with customer-managed KMS.
- Integrations: you plan to use our SDK for generation + embedding calls; will need server-side auth (service keys) and routing rules between low-latency chat and cost-optimized reranker pipelines.

Open technical questions we agreed to follow up on:
1) SDK setup + auth: recommended service key rotation, mTLS options?

3) Structured output / tool calling: Desire strongly-typed responses for action extraction and a tool-calling pattern for DB lookups.
4) Embeddings + reranker: batching, nearest-neighbor throughput, GPU/CPU tradeoffs for index refreshing.
5) Dedicated capacity sizing: autoscaling policy (min/max nodes), per-GPU concurrency limits, queue depth recommendations for smoothing bursts.

Next steps (proposed):

Hi all —

Thanks for the details, Anika. Answers and recommendations below (long, but wanted to be concrete):

1) SDK setup & auth- Pattern: server-side service keys + short-lived tokens. We recommend using our service key to mint short-lived tokens (15m TTL) for each session; rotate service keys quarterly.
- mTLS: supported for control-plane connections to the Private control plane. Data-plane supports TLS with client certs on request (we can enable at provisioning and wire into your KMS).
- Example (NodeJS pseudo):
  const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ baseURL: 'https://dedicated-east.redwood.ai', auth: { bearer: process.env.SESSION_TOKEN } });
  // generation with structured output  const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-chat-l', input: prompt, tool_call: true, schema: 'https://example.com/schemas/action-v1.json' });

2) Routing / model variants- Use request headers to indicate route: X-Route: chat-lowlatency OR X-Route: search-highthroughput. Redwood routing rules can map headers to model families and capacity tiers; fallback to cheaper model variants on saturation.

3) Structured output / tool calling- We surface a strict JSON schema parameter on the generate call (schema URL or inline). The runtime validates and returns a JSON blob in the top-level 'structured_output' field (machine-parseable). Example schema recommended: a top-level object with action:string, args:object, confidence:float. We also support streaming structured blocks for large outputs.

4) Embeddings & reranker- Batch embeddings: use batches of 256-1024 depending on GPU memory and sequence length. For nightly 10k jobs, prefer sharded parallel batch jobs using the dedicated embedding workers (CPU-backed with GPU fallback for high-throughput).
- Reranker: run on GPU where latency required; for bulk reranks, queue and run on high-throughput nodes.
- Index refreshes: support incremental upserts to the vector DB; avoid full rebuilds by periodically re-embedding changed docs and issuing partial re-index jobs.

5) Dedicated capacity sizing / autoscaling guidance- Baseline numbers (estimate; we'll refine after we see the KPIs file):
  - Chat (low-latency): target per-GPU concurrency 4-8 for p95 < 120ms (short prompts). For 250 steady QPS, estimate ~250 / (4 * tokens-per-second-per-GPU) — ballpark 6-8 GPUs minimum.
  - Peak buffer: autoscaler min: 6 GPUs, max: 40 GPUs (supports 1,200 QPS bursts).
  - Reranker/embeddings pool: separate worker pool. For nightly 10k embedding jobs, schedule off-peak or use burst capacity.
  - Queue depth: set in-flight queue per pool to 2x expected burst (e.g., chat queue depth 2,400 for 1,200 peak) and use dequeue smoothing window of 30s to avoid flapping.
  - Autoscaler smoothing: use a 60-120s moving average with cooldown 120s. Aggressive scaling on sustained load, conservative on short spikes.
  - Concurrency limits: per-request policy enforced at the runtime; set per-GPU concurrent requests cap + token-based cost budget.

6) Example autoscaling config (YAML pseudo):
  pool: chat-lowlatency
  instance_type: a100-40gb
  min_replicas: 6
  max_replicas: 40
  target_utilization: 0.7
  smoothing_window_seconds: 60
  cooldown_seconds: 120
  queue_depth: 2400

Attachments referenced: redwood-dedicated-architecture.pdf (diagram), SLA_Draft_v2.docx (SLA template). I've attached a compact sizing note and sample SDK snippet.
